key_insight: A hybrid front-surface silicon nanocone plus absorber-embedded nanohole structure improves light trapping, reduces reflection, and boosts thin-film silicon solar-cell efficiency.
engineering_relevance: The design offers a practical optical-architecture strategy for raising current generation and thermal robustness in thin-film photovoltaics without changing the base material system.
method: FDTD simulations used to optimize nanocone and nanohole geometry for optical absorption.
Electrical device modeling coupled with the optical results to estimate Jsc, Voc, fill factor, and efficiency.
Opto-electro-thermal analysis assessed performance under non-isothermal conditions up to 45°C.
evidence_signal: The optimized device achieved 34.64 mA cm-2 Jsc, 0.82 V Voc, 86.27% fill factor, and 24.42% efficiency, with 95.21% efficiency retained at 45°C and a 17.74% gain over a nanohole-only design.
watch_item: Fabrication complexity and alignment of the hybrid nanocone-nanohole nanostructure may be challenging to implement at scale.
paper_title: Hybrid Nanocone-Nanohole Light Trapping for High-Efficiency Thin-Film Silicon Solar Cells
